Code facts confirmed in /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215:
- products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126-139 dispatches `_start_stamphog_review` on every TaskRun save that reaches that point with `pr_url` set and the toggle on; there is no dispatch-side dedupe (contrast the ReviewHog leg, which collapses via a deterministic workflow id, receivers.py:77-78).
- products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149-155 is a plain `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)` per call.
- products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1138-1147 pays a writer-pinned StamphogRepoConfig lookup and tasks.py:1159 a GitHub `get_pr` BEFORE the head-keyed dedupe (tasks.py:1198+), and 1160-1162 retries on GitHubRateLimitError with countdown >= 60s. So each refire with an unchanged head is a broker publish + DB read + one GitHub GET that ends in a no-op.
- The refire is reachable: products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:229-235 (`_record_run_pr_merged`) writes `output.pr_merged` with `update_fields=["output","updated_at"]` (webhooks.py:292) while `pr_url` is already present, which passes the receiver's guard at receivers.py:86 and re-dispatches the stamphog task, whose fetch then finds the PR not open (tasks.py:1166-1169) and exits. That is one guaranteed wasted GET per merged inbox PR. products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2149-2154 (`set_task_run_output`) also preserves an existing `pr_url` and saves `output` on every agent-server set_output call.
votes.refutation:
Attempted refutation narrows the finding substantially and removes the should_fix priority:
1. Frequency premise is overstated. The receiver early-exits on any save whose `update_fields` lacks "output" (receivers.py:85-89). Every other TaskRun save in non-test code uses update_fields without "output" (facade/api.py:2075 status/state, :2256 artifacts, :3146/:4594 mcp servers, :3347; temporal/client.py:76; update_task_run_status.py:69; models.py:471/502/745/1263) and no bare `run.save()` on a TaskRun exists under products/tasks/backend. Only two writers touch `output`: `set_task_run_output`/PATCH (agent server, per receivers.py:28-29 fired when the branch changed or the PR opened, so a refire there mostly carries a new head that legitimately needs review) and the webhook writes, which are idempotent per key (webhooks.py:283-289) so they fire at most once for `pr_url` and once for `pr_merged`. Refires "over the run's lifetime" are therefore a handful per run, not a per-save hot path.
2. The cost is a documented, deliberate tradeoff: receivers.py:75-79 states "a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)", and tasks.py:1124-1128 explains the head-keyed dedupe is intentionally post-fetch so a refire after a lost `synchronize` delivery still reviews new commits.
3. The suggested fix (dispatch-side TTL cache keyed on pr_url) would suppress that lost-synchronize backstop within the window, so it is not a free win.
What survives: one guaranteed no-op Celery task + GitHub GET per merged inbox PR (the pr_merged webhook write), plus occasional same-head refires from the agent server. Real but minor and bounded; no user-visible effect. consider, not should_fix.

votes.evidence: Mechanics the finding describes are accurate: receivers.py:126-139 dispatches `_start_stamphog_review` on every qualifying output save with no dispatch-side dedupe, and tasks.py:1136-1159 pays a write-DB repo-config lookup plus a GitHub `get_pr` before the head-keyed dedupe at tasks.py:1198-1216. But the premise that these refires "repeat over the run's lifetime while the PR follow-up loop babysits the PR" is contradicted by the code: (1) receivers.py:85-88 drops any save whose declared `update_fields` omits "output", and the follow-up loop persists `state`, not `output` (facade api.py:2049-2056 adds only the keys the PATCH carries; test_inbox_trigger.py:181-189 asserts status/state saves do not re-fire); (2) the webhook backstop `_record_run_output_field` (webhooks.py:284-289) returns False without saving when the key is already set, so `pr_url` is written exactly once and `pr_merged` once more, and that single merged-PR refire exits at tasks.py:1166-1169 after one GET; (3) the remaining repeat writer is the agent server's set_output/PATCH (facade api.py:2139-2154), which per receivers.py:28-30 fires at the end of turns whose branch changed, i.e. mostly with a new head where the GitHub fetch is needed anyway. The per-refire cost is an explicitly accepted design: receivers.py:75-79 docstring states "a same-head re-trigger costs one fetch (early-exit)", and tasks.py:1124-1128 + 1155-1157 document that the fetch runs before the dedupe on purpose because only GitHub knows the current head and a refire is the only recovery for a lost `synchronize` delivery. That backstop is covered by `test_inbox_receiver_leg_refires_dedupe_on_the_current_head` (stamphog test_tasks.py:992-1027, case "missed_webhook_head_gets_reviewed"). The suggested short-TTL cache keyed on pr_url would suppress exactly that case for pushes landing inside the window, trading a tested recovery path for a few saved GETs. `get_pr` (github_client.py:466-474) has no ETag caching, so each refire is one real API call, but with the writer set above that is a handful of calls per PR, not a sustained drain.
votes.refutation: Attempted to confirm an unbounded refire loop and failed: the follow-up loop's saves never carry `output` in `update_fields` and are dropped at receivers.py:85-88; the webhook backstop is idempotent and writes `pr_url` once; the only repeat source (agent-server output sync) mostly coincides with a head change where the fetch is productive. The one-fetch-per-refire cost is documented as intentional in both the receiver docstring and the task docstring, and the head-first ordering exists to back-stop a lost synchronize webhook, which an existing parameterized test pins. The finding is therefore an efficiency observation about a deliberate, bounded, tested tradeoff whose proposed fix would weaken that tested backstop, not a defect.

votes.evidence: Mechanism is as described (no dispatch-side dedupe): receivers.py:126-139 queues `_start_stamphog_review` on every `output` save carrying `pr_url`, and `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1138-1159) pays a write-DB config lookup then a GitHub `get_pr` before the head-keyed dedupe. But the finding's premise that "these saves repeat over the run's lifetime" is not reachable from any write path in this repo. TaskRun.output has exactly two writers: (1) `set_task_run_output` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2139-2154), called by the agent server's PATCH `set_output` (presentation/views/api.py:1107), which per DECISIONS.md:2553-2554 syncs only at the end of an agent turn whose git branch changed, and on PR open - after the PR exists the branch is stable, and a turn that moves the head makes the fetch feed a genuine review, not a no-op; (2) the webhook backstop `_record_run_output_field` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:276-295), which is idempotent per key and writes `pr_url` once (line 212) and `pr_merged` once (line 235), so it contributes at most ONE refire per PR, and at that moment the PR is merged so the task exits at tasks.py:1166-1169 after a single fetch. Status / follow-up-loop persistence saves use `update_fields` without `output` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/update_task_run_status.py:40) and are dropped at receivers.py:85-89 before any DB hit. Reachability is further narrowed by two prod gates: the acting reviewer's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle defaults False (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:294), and without a synced+enabled StamphogRepoConfig the task returns at tasks.py:1151-1153 before any GitHub call. Net production cost per PR: roughly one wasted `get_pr` (the pr_merged refire) plus at most a couple of branch-metadata resyncs - not a per-save hot loop and not enough to move the installation token's rate budget.
votes.refutation: Tried to find a write path that saves `output` with an unchanged `pr_url` repeatedly: none exists in this repo. Webhook writes are once-per-key idempotent, temporal status writes exclude `output` from `update_fields` and are filtered at receivers.py:86, and the only remaining writer (agent-server set_output) is documented as branch-change-gated. The head-keyed dedupe in the task is also a deliberate design (tasks.py:1124-1128: a refire after a lost `synchronize` delivery still reviews the new head), and the proposed short-TTL dispatch cache would suppress exactly that backstop during its window. With the trigger bounded to ~1-2 cheap calls per PR lifetime and the suggested fix trading away a documented safeguard, this is a speculative efficiency note whose central premise (continuous refires) the code contradicts, so it is not a real defect.
